# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 65

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 65:1 "torments every such person according to his deeds" vs. "in proportion to his deeds"

- **EMET:** "torments every such person according to his deeds"
- **LOGOS:** "torments every such person in proportion to his deeds"
- **PNEUMA:** "afflicts each person in proportion to what they deserve"
- **Greek:** *kata ta erga autou basanizei* — torments according to his works
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "torments every such person in proportion to his deeds" (LOGOS). "In proportion to" captures *kata* (according to/in proportion to) better; PNEUMA's "what they deserve" adds judgment language not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 65:1 "great sinner" vs. "one who has sinned greatly"

- **EMET:** "one who sins receives many torments"
- **LOGOS:** "the great sinner receives many torments"
- **PNEUMA:** "Those who have sinned greatly receive many torments"
- **Greek:** *ho pollā hamartanōn pollas basanous* — the one sinning greatly receives many torments
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the great sinner receives many torments" (LOGOS). The participle *pollā hamartanōn* = sinning greatly/abundantly; "great sinner" is a compact rendering.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 65:2 "worthy to suffer" vs. "worthy to undergo"

- **EMET:** "sufferings that he is worthy to suffer"
- **LOGOS:** "sufferings that this person is worthy to undergo"
- **PNEUMA:** "suffering they are deserving of"
- **Greek:** *pathēmata hōn axios estin* — sufferings which he is worthy of
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "sufferings that this person is worthy to undergo" (LOGOS). "Undergo" is more general than "suffer" (tautological) and avoids redundancy.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 65:2 "losses of money and goods" — all agree

- **EMET:** "various losses and losses of money and goods"
- **LOGOS:** "various losses and losses of money and goods"
- **PNEUMA:** "various losses: loss of money, loss of possessions"
- **Note:** All three agree substantially.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "various losses and losses of money and goods." The repetition of *apoleia* (loss) is characteristic of Hermas's style.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 65:3 "not through any malice" vs. "not from any hatred or malice"

- **EMET:** "not through any malice toward the person"
- **LOGOS:** "not from any malice toward the person"
- **PNEUMA:** "not from any hatred or malice"
- **Greek:** *ouk apo kakoētheias* — not from malice/ill-will
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not from any malice toward the person" (EMET adjusted). *Kakoētheia* = malice/ill-will; single term; PNEUMA adds "hatred" not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 65:3 "the Lord loves him and hastens therefore to chastise him"

- **EMET:** "the Lord loves him and hastens therefore to chastise him"
- **LOGOS:** "since the Lord loves him, he hastens to chastise him"
- **PNEUMA:** "Because God loves them, God hastens to discipline them"
- **Note:** Agreement on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "since the Lord loves him, he hastens to chastise him" (LOGOS). "Chastise" preserves the formal disciplinary term *paideuein*; "discipline" (PNEUMA) is a valid synonym.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 65:3 "purified of the great iniquity that is in him"

- **EMET:** "purified of the great iniquity that is in him"
- **LOGOS:** "purified of the great iniquity that is in him"
- **PNEUMA:** "purified from the deep iniquity that is in them"
- **Greek:** *katharisthēi apo tēs pollēs anomias* — purified from the great lawlessness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "purified of the great iniquity that is in him." EMET and LOGOS agree; *pollēs* = great/much (not "deep"); PNEUMA adds an interpretive coloring.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 65:4 "reflect on their iniquities" vs. "think about their iniquities"

- **EMET:** "they think about their iniquities and their evil deeds, and repent"
- **LOGOS:** "they reflect on their iniquities and evil deeds, and repent"
- **PNEUMA:** "they think back on their sins and evil deeds and repent"
- **Greek:** *enthymountai tas anomias...kai metanoousi* — they think on/reflect on their iniquities and repent
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they reflect on their iniquities and evil deeds, and repent" (LOGOS). "Reflect on" captures *enthymeomai* (deliberate reflection) better than "think about."

---

## Disagreement 9 — 65:5 "has nothing and has no power against" vs. "has nothing in himself to resist"

- **EMET:** "the soul of the man who has nothing and has no power against the angel"
- **LOGOS:** "the man who has nothing in himself and has no resistance against the angel"
- **PNEUMA:** "a person who has nothing within themselves to resist the angel"
- **Greek:** *ho anthrōpos mēden echōn en heautō kai mē dunamenos antistēnai* — the person having nothing in himself and not being able to resist
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the man who has nothing in himself and has no resistance against the angel of punishment" (LOGOS). The two conditions (*nothing in him* and *cannot resist*) both need to be stated.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 65.*
